disposition_reason: Mean Zn, Pb, Cd, Cu, Hg and Co concentrations by AAS in two edible clays (Nzu, Ulo) from four Onitsha markets are printed in Tables 2-7.

study.market: Ochanja, Ose, Relief and Okpoko markets, Onitsha, Anambra State, Nigeria

period.as_reported: Samples were purchased between 25th April and 6th May, 2013 (analysis June to October 2013)

study.method: Flame AAS (FS240) after aqua regia digestion of oven-dried (100 °C) clay
study.qa: Calibration with commercial stock standards; no CRM or recovery reported

controls.control: clay type (bentonite Ulo vs kaolin Nzu)
controls.outcome: Zn 2.737 vs 10.332 ppm (P = .000); Co 0.004 vs 0.308 ppm (P = .003); Pb, Cd, Cu, Hg not significantly different

unresolved: n = 3 is described as replicate measurements; it is unclear whether three separate purchases per market were analyzed individually or pooled.
Market and type means appear to treat ND as zero.
Copper table means do not reconcile with their cells (see integrity flags).
Cd type 11 mean SD (0.130) equals the type 1 SD, possibly a copy error.
The manifest DOI (10.9734/bjast/2014/7946) is not printed in the PDF; title, journal, volume 4(14) and pages 2114-2124 match.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: FAO/WHO permissible limits in food as cited
